qAndA.answer: The mathematical notation for a subset is a 'C' symbol with a line underneath.
qAndA.question: What is the mathematical notation for a subset?

qAndA.answer: The mathematical notation for a set that is not a subset of another set is a 'C' symbol with a slash through it.
qAndA.question: What is the mathematical notation for a set that is not a subset of another set?

qAndA.answer: Set D is a subset of set A because all the elements of D are also found in A. The definition of a subset does not exclude sets that are equal.
qAndA.question: Why is set D a subset of set A even though they are equal?

qAndA.answer: Set A is written on the chalkboard at the top of the screen throughout the video.
qAndA.question: How does the video visually represent set A?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Welcome to the World Wide Center of Mathematics College Algebra series.
So today I'm going to be talking about subsets and this is a continuation of our set video
which you can find in our College Algebra playlist.
So what I have behind me is a defined set A with elements 1, 2, 5, 8, 17 and 102.
And these don't have any real relationship with each other, they're just numbers that I picked.
And so a subset, a subset is defined to be a set whose elements are found in another set.
So for example, let's look at a subset lowercase A. We'll set this equal to 1, 2, 5.
And so our definition is that the elements of a subset can be found in a different set.
And so we've got elements 1, 2 and 5 in set lowercase A.
And each of these can be found in our defined capital A set.
So this is a subset of A. So this subset is a subset of capital A.
And so let's look at another one. We'll do B this time.
So B has elements 1, 8, 17, 102.
And each of these elements can be found in set A. So B is a subset of A.
And now let's look at another subset.
We can do C. And C is equal to 1, 2, 3, 17.
And so here, it's pretty obvious. We've got a 3 in our set C.
And 3 is not found in A. So C is not a subset of A.
This is the notation for when your set is not a subset of another set.
And so what if we had, let's try set D.
What if we had set D with elements 1, 2, 5, 8, 17 and 102.
So set D has all of the elements that are in set A.
In fact, set D is equal to A.
But let's look at our definition of a subset again.
A subset is any set whose elements are found in another set.
And so all of the elements of set D are found in set A.
So D is still a subset of A.
And this one has notation that is a little different than the other sets.
Because it's also equal to set A, we use our subset symbol as well as a line underneath.
So D is a subset of A.
Thank you for watching this Worldwide Center of Mathematics short on algebra.
